classes.title: Storms 101
classes.subtitle: Thunderstorms, tornadoes, hurricanes & blizzards — and how we stay safe
classes.description: Four wild-weather weeks: thunderstorms, tornadoes, hurricanes and blizzards. What makes each storm special and the one safety rule every kid should know — every lesson ends on 'here's how we stay safe,' never on the scary part.

lessons.title: Thunderstorms: When Thunder Roars, Go Indoors
Hurricanes: Giant Storms From the Ocean
Blizzards: Snow, Wind & Staying Warm — Graduation!

long_description: Some kids hide from thunder. Cane teaches them to understand it instead. Storms 101 is four short weekly video lessons where Cane the Weather Dog and his daddy (a real TV meteorologist and Four-Time National Emmy Award Winner!) meet the four big storms: thunderstorms, tornadoes, hurricanes and blizzards — what makes each one special, and the one safety rule every kid should know for each.

Every lesson is sized for K–2 attention spans and every single one ends the same way: "here's how we stay safe." That's a promise we make to parents. Kids leave this class less afraid of storms, not more, because scary noises stop being scary once you understand them. The final week reviews all four storms and their safety rules, and your child earns an official Storms 101 graduation diploma.

Each week also comes with six printables: a parent & teacher guide, a reading, homework, an activity sheet, a student handout and a quiz. One price covers up to 4 kids in your house — perfect for siblings who want to learn together.

classes.title: Hurricane Hunters
classes.subtitle: Fly into the storm with Cane
classes.description: How hurricanes are born over warm ocean water, how scientists fly INTO them to keep us safe, and how families make a hurricane plan together.

lessons.title: Hurricane Hunters: Scientists Who Fly In
Watches, Warnings, and What They Mean
Storm Surge: Why We Move Away From Water

long_description: Did you know there are scientists who fly airplanes INTO hurricanes on purpose? That fact alone hooks every kid who takes this class. Hurricane Hunters is six video lessons where Cane explores how hurricanes are born over warm ocean water, what the eye of the storm really is, and how the bravest scientists in the sky gather the data that keeps families safe.

Your child's teacher isn't reading from a script — he's a meteorologist and Four-Time National Emmy Award Winner who has covered hurricanes on live television for years. He knows what watches and warnings actually mean, why we move away from the water when storm surge comes, and how to explain all of it so a first grader feels informed instead of frightened.

The class ends with the most practical homework in our catalog: your family makes its own hurricane plan together, guided step by step. If you live anywhere a hurricane can reach — and especially if you don't and your kids only see them on the news — this class turns big scary storms into something your child understands.

classes.title: Cane's Weather Academy
classes.subtitle: The full weather adventure — 8 weeks
classes.description: Cane's flagship K–4 course: an eight-week journey through everything weather — the sun, the water cycle, clouds, rain and snow, wind, the seasons, and forecasting like a real meteorologist.
long_description: This is Cane's flagship — the full weather adventure. Eight weeks, eight video lessons, one big journey through everything the sky does: what weather is, how the Sun drives it, the water cycle, clouds, rain and snow, wind and air, the four seasons, and finally how real meteorologists put it all together to make a forecast.

Each week unlocks a new lesson with Cane and his daddy, plus six printables: a parent & teacher guide, a reading, homework, an activity sheet, a student handout and a quiz. The pacing matches a homeschool planner perfectly: one lesson, one week, no falling behind.

And the finale is something special: Be a Meteorologist, where your child uses real weather tools and everything from Weeks 1–7 to make their own forecast — just like Cane's daddy does on TV — and earns a Weather Academy graduation certificate. It's also a big step toward Cane's graduation gift: finish every Cane's class and your family unlocks a free EarthSphere Academy class for grades 5–12.

classes.title: The Sun & Our Weather
classes.subtitle: The star that runs the show
classes.description: Why the Sun is the engine of all our weather — day and night, seasons, and sun safety.

lessons.title: How the Sun Makes Wind and Rain
Sun Safety: Protecting Our Skin and Eyes

long_description: Everything in our sky starts with one star. The Sun & Our Weather is six bright, friendly video lessons about the engine that runs it all: why we have day and night, where shadows come from, how sunshine stirs up wind and rain, and why the seasons change as Earth makes its big trip around the Sun.

Cane and his daddy — a real meteorologist and Four-Time National Emmy Award Winner — keep it concrete and playful for K–5 kids: shadow experiments to try in the backyard, sky-watching habits, and the kind of "why?" answers that turn car-ride questions into science. There's a full lesson on sun safety too: protecting skin and eyes, the smart way, without making the Sun the bad guy.

The final lesson introduces solar scientists — the people whose whole job is watching our star — so kids learn early that science is something real people do every day. App included free, whole household covered, one lesson a week.

classes.title: Volcanoes & Earthquakes
classes.subtitle: When the Earth rumbles
classes.description: Inside our planet: why volcanoes erupt, why the ground shakes, and how scientists monitor and warn so people stay safe.

lessons.title: A Journey to the Center of the Earth
The Scientists Who Listen to the Earth
Drop, Cover, Hold On: Our Safety Plan

long_description: When the Earth rumbles, curious kids want to know why — and that's exactly the right instinct. Volcanoes & Earthquakes takes 3rd–5th graders on a journey to the center of the Earth: what's down there, how giant plates move, why volcanoes wake up, and what's really happening when the ground shakes.

Your kids' guide is an environmental geoscientist (with the master's degree to prove it) who also happens to be Cane's daddy — so the science is real, and the telling is fun. A full lesson is devoted to the scientists who listen to the Earth with their instruments, watching and warning so people have time to get safe. That's the through-line of every Cane's class: scientists monitor, scientists warn, families prepare.

The final lesson is Drop, Cover, Hold On — your family's earthquake plan, practiced together. Six lessons, about 25 minutes each, with study guides, flash cards, games, and quizzes in the free companion app.

classes.title: Our Amazing Ocean
classes.subtitle: Waves, currents, and tsunami science
classes.description: The ocean that covers most of our planet — currents, waves, sea life zones, and how warning centers watch for tsunamis to keep coasts safe.

lessons.title: Tsunamis and the Scientists Who Watch
Ocean Heroes: Keeping Our Sea Healthy

long_description: The ocean covers most of our planet, makes most of our weather, and most kids have never been taught how it works. Our Amazing Ocean fixes that: six video lessons for 3rd–5th graders on currents (rivers in the sea!), waves and tides, and how the ocean and the sky work together to build the weather over your house — explained by a meteorologist who forecasts that connection for a living.

There's a lesson on tsunamis, handled the Cane's way: what they are, why they happen, and most importantly, the warning centers and scientists who watch the ocean day and night so coastal families get time to move to safety. Kids come away knowing the system protects them — not just that big waves exist.
The class closes with Ocean Heroes — what kids can actually do to keep our sea healthy. Six lessons, free companion app with games and quizzes, and one price for every kid in your house.

classes.title: Cane's Earth Explorers
classes.subtitle: The whole-planet adventure — 8 weeks
classes.description: Cane's big earth-science course: inside the planet, volcanoes, floods, wildfires, drought, oceans, the Sun, and our changing climate — each week ending with how scientists and families stay safe.

lessons.title: Our Changing Climate — and the Helpers

long_description: Cane's Earth Explorers is the big one — eight weeks across the whole planet. Inside the Earth, volcanoes and earthquakes, floods and the water cycle, wildfires, drought, oceans and currents, the Sun, and our changing climate. It's the widest adventure in Cane's catalog, built for curious 3rd–5th graders who ask the big questions.

Every hazard week follows the rule this school was founded on: we always end on how scientists and families stay safe. Wildfire week ends with the firefighters and forecasters who protect us. Flood week ends with how warnings work. The climate week ends with the helpers — the scientists and problem-solvers working on it right now. Kids finish braver and smarter, never scared.

Taught by a meteorologist, environmental geoscientist and Four-Time National Emmy Award Winner, with a new lesson unlocking each week and the full companion app included free. Finish Earth Explorers along with Cane's other classes and your family earns Cane's graduation gift: a free class at EarthSphere Academy, our school for grades 5–12.
